Thanks for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we all stay aligned.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goals: validate latency SLOs (p95/p99) and sustained throughput (tokens/sec) vs your current hyperscaler endpoints (Vertex AI / Bedrock).
- Important to measure both end-to-end and infra-only (no CDN), plus cold-start behavior and concurrency characteristics.
- Typical prompt profiles: short (chat prompts ~32 tokens), medium (1–2 paragraph context ~256 tokens), and long (docs ~1024 tokens).
- Success criteria: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (if feasible), predictable p99 tail, and >= X tokens/sec for your baseline throughput needs (we'll calibrate exact target once you share baseline).

Proposed next steps:
1) Dev to propose a test config (models, batch sizes, sequence lengths, measurement points).
2) Run A/B: Redwood hosted API vs Vertex AI endpoint (same model family where possible) across the three prompt profiles.
3) Capture metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, concurrency scaling, cold-start latency, GPU utilization, and memory/KV-cache hit rates.
4) Share raw results + summary deck; schedule 30-min follow-up to review.

Timeline suggestion: start tests next Wednesday, run 2–3 days, share results by the following Monday. We can accelerate if you have preferred test windows.

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and matches our ask. A couple of clarifications so Dev can tune the test config: 

- For performance targets we want both infra-only (request reaches model container) and end-to-end (including our VPC egress and any fronting LB). Can you include both measurements?

- For tokens/sec, we care about sustained throughput at our standard concurrency (20 concurrent streams) and at peak (100 concurrent streams).

We're currently evaluating both Vertex and Bedrock; please make sure the A/B compares against Vertex running the same model family (if possible) and note any differences in quantization/precision.

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks, below is a proposed test config we suggest for an apples-to-apples A/B: 

High level A/B approach:
- A: Redwood hosted API (same model family, quantization where supported)
- B: Vertex AI endpoint (customer-provided model or closest comparable)

Scenarios (run each for steady-state and cold-start):
1) Short prompts: 32 tokens output target, 1–3 token generation bursts (chat-like)
2) Medium prompts: 256 tokens output target (paragraph generation)
3) Long prompts: 1024 tokens output target (document completion)

Measurement points:
- p50, p95, p99 latency (ms) — end-to-end and infra-only
- tokens/sec sustained over 60s windows
- concurrency scaling curve (1, 5, 20, 50, 100 concurrent streams)
- cold-start: time from 0 replicas to first token delivered under varying concurrency
- resource metrics: GPU utilization, memory, tokenization overhead, KV-cache hit rate

Suggested infra/config details:
- Model variants: base and quantized (if supported) — note exact precision (FP16 / int8)
- Batch sizes: dynamic batching with max batch 64 for short, 16 for medium/long; also test single-stream (no batching)
- Sequence length caps: 2k for long tests; measure truncated vs full-run behavior
- Warmup: 30s warmup phase before measurements; repeat each test 3x and report medians

Attachments:
- [Attachment: test-config.yaml] (full test harness config)

Notes: Redwood's runtime includes prefix/KV caching and a continuous batcher — for workloads with repeated context (e.g., system/prompt prefixes) we typically see tokens/sec improvements vs naive endpoints. We'll instrument KV-cache hit rate so you can see the delta.

I can run the tests from our side if you prefer; otherwise we can share the harness and you can run from your VPC to include your end-to-end network. Which do you prefer?

—Dev
